source.title: Population estimates and components of population change. Detailed time series 2011 to 2025 England and Wales, local authorities, sex and age
source.published: The data tables in this spreadsheet were originally published at 9.30am 29 July 2026.
source.nextPublication: The next publication is scheduled for summer 2027.
source.geography: Local authorities in England and Wales as of April 2023

definitions.births: Estimated number of births occurring in the twelve months to mid-year
definitions.deaths: Estimated number of deaths occurring in the twelve months to mid-year
definitions.internalIn: Estimated in moves originating elsewhere in the UK during the twelve months to mid-year
definitions.internalOut: Estimated out moves terminating elsewhere in the UK during the twelve months to mid-year
definitions.internationalIn: Estimated international immigration moves originating from outside the UK during the twelve months to midyear
definitions.internationalOut: Estimated international emigration moves terminating outside the UK during the twelve months to mid-year
definitions.other: Includes estimated net effect of changes to special populations during the twelve months to mid-year. Special populations comprise prisoner, armed forces and their overseas based dependent populations. Also includes estimated population change not attributed to a specific cause in the twelve months to mid-year and small adjustments necessary to account for issues such as minor LA boundary changes and large postcode areas that overlap LA boundaries. For 2012 to 2021 other_change also includes unattributable population change introduced after the rebasing of the Mid-year estimates to be consistent with the 2021 census.

usage: Components of change in the usual resident population, each for the twelve months to 30 June. `population` has one value per year in `years`; each flow has one value per year after the first, so flow index i is the change from years[i] to years[i + 1]. Values are exactly as published. For every area and year, population[i] + births - deaths + (internalIn - internalOut) + (internationalIn - internationalOut) + other = population[i + 1].
